_doc: The second cities and heritage towns of Europe — the places worth the detour that the first pass through each country misses, plus two of the great classical sites.

destinations.name: Assisi & Umbria
destinations.blurb: Tuscany without the queues — hill towns of pink stone above olive terraces, Giotto's frescoes in the basilica at Assisi, and Orvieto's cathedral front rising out of a tufa cliff.

destinations.name: Genoa & the Ligurian Riviera
destinations.blurb: A working port with the densest medieval quarter in Europe behind it — dark alleys opening onto palace courtyards — and the whole Riviera within an hour either side, Portofino one way, the French border the other.

destinations.name: Ravenna & the Adriatic
destinations.blurb: Eight small brick buildings holding the best Byzantine mosaics anywhere outside Istanbul — gold ceilings, a starry blue vault over Galla Placidia — in a flat, cyclable town with Dante's tomb and the beach twenty minutes away.

destinations.name: Bergamo & Lake Iseo
destinations.blurb: A walled Venetian upper town on a hill reached by funicular, looking out at the Alps on one side and the Lombard plain on the other — and a quieter lake next door that the coach parties have not found.

destinations.name: Salamanca
destinations.blurb: Built entirely from a sandstone that turns gold at sunset, around the oldest university in Spain — which means a town of plateresque facades that is also full of students, and busiest at midnight.

destinations.name: Cáceres & Extremadura
destinations.blurb: A walled town of stone towers and storks' nests where nothing has been built since the sixteenth century, in Spain's emptiest and cheapest corner — with Roman Mérida down the road and the best ham in the country from the oak pasture around it.

destinations.name: Zaragoza & Aragón
destinations.blurb: A vast riverside basilica with domes painted by Goya, a Moorish palace beneath a Christian one, and the Pyrenees two hours north — a real Spanish city that almost no visitor stops in, halfway between Madrid and Barcelona.

destinations.name: Carcassonne & Cathar Country
destinations.blurb: A double-walled citadel with fifty-two towers, restored in the nineteenth century into the definitive picture of a medieval fortress — and behind it a country of ruined castles on knife-edge ridges where the Cathars were besieged out of existence.

destinations.name: Reims & Champagne
destinations.blurb: The cathedral where French kings were crowned, with Chagall windows in the apse, standing over miles of Roman chalk cellars where the champagne houses age their bottles — and the vineyards themselves half an hour south.

destinations.name: Toulouse
destinations.blurb: Built entirely of pink brick, which at dusk goes the colour of terracotta — a student and aerospace city on the Garonne with the biggest Romanesque church in Europe and a cassoulet worth the afternoon it takes to recover from.

destinations.name: Kutná Hora
destinations.blurb: Medieval Bohemia's silver town, rich enough to build a cathedral to miners — and, in a suburb chapel, an ossuary where a nineteenth-century woodcarver arranged forty thousand people's bones into a chandelier.

destinations.name: Olomouc
destinations.blurb: The second-biggest heritage reserve in the country and barely a tour group in it — six baroque fountains, a plague column the size of a house, and a university town's worth of cheap beer underneath it all.
photos: Olomouc upper square town hall astronomical clock

destinations.name: Lublin & Zamość
destinations.blurb: A castle chapel covered in Russo-Byzantine frescoes painted for a Catholic king, an old town of painted merchant houses, and an hour south the only Renaissance ideal city ever actually finished — with Majdanek on the edge of town, left exactly as it was.

destinations.name: Malbork & the Vistula
destinations.blurb: The largest castle in the world by land area, a red-brick fortress-monastery the Teutonic Knights ran their state from — half a million square metres of it, on a river bend an hour from Gdańsk.

destinations.name: Maastricht
destinations.blurb: The least Dutch city in the Netherlands — Roman, Catholic, hilly and closer to Brussels than Amsterdam, with a bookshop in a gothic church and miles of defensive tunnels cut into the marl beneath it.

destinations.name: Delft & Leiden
destinations.blurb: The two canal towns everybody skips on the way between Amsterdam and Rotterdam — Vermeer's Delft, still recognisably his, with the blue pottery still being made; and Leiden, oldest university in the country, Rembrandt's birthplace, and more canal per square mile than Amsterdam.

destinations.name: Dinant & the Ardennes
destinations.blurb: A citadel on a cliff over the Meuse with a bulb-domed church wedged underneath it, in the birthplace of the saxophone — and behind it a forested upland of castles, caves and rivers you can kayak down.

destinations.name: Bern
destinations.blurb: A capital that looks like a small town — four miles of arcaded sandstone streets inside a loop of the Aare, an astronomical clock, Einstein's flat, and locals who swim the river home from work in summer.
photos: Bern rose garden view old town

destinations.name: Basel
destinations.blurb: Where Switzerland, Germany and France meet on the Rhine — nearly forty museums for two hundred thousand people, a red sandstone minster over the river, and a ferry pulled across the current by the current itself.
photos: Basel Marktplatz Rathaus red town hall

destinations.name: The Wachau Valley
destinations.blurb: Twenty-four miles of Danube between two abbeys, terraced with apricot orchards and Grüner Veltliner vines, a ruined castle where Richard the Lionheart was held, and a baroque monastery at Melk with a library worth the trip on its own.

destinations.name: Eger & the Danube Bend
destinations.blurb: A baroque town under a castle that held off the Ottomans, with the northernmost Turkish minaret still standing and a valley of cellars cut into rhyolite outside it selling Bull's Blood straight from the barrel.
photos: Valley of the Beautiful Women wine cellars Eger

destinations.name: Sibiu & the Saxon Villages
destinations.blurb: A German town in the middle of Romania, with attic vents in the roofs that look like half-closed eyes watching the square — and around it fortified Saxon churches in villages that eight hundred years of history nearly emptied.
photos: Sibiu Large Square eyes of the city

destinations.name: Košice
destinations.blurb: The easternmost gothic cathedral in Europe, at the head of a long spindle-shaped square lined with pastel townhouses and a singing fountain — a city of a quarter of a million that sees almost no visitors at all.

destinations.name: Coimbra
destinations.blurb: Portugal's old capital, stacked up a hill above the Mondego around a university with a gilded baroque library kept cool by a colony of bats that eat the bookworms — and its own darker, male-voiced kind of fado.

destinations.name: Zagori & the Vikos Gorge
destinations.blurb: The Greece nobody books — forty-six stone villages in the Pindus mountains linked by arched packhorse bridges, above the deepest gorge in the world relative to its width, with bears and wolves still in the forest.
photos: Papingo village Zagori Epirus stone houses

destinations.name: The Aran Islands & the Burren
destinations.blurb: A limestone pavement full of Arctic and Mediterranean flowers growing side by side in the cracks, and three islands off the end of it where a prehistoric fort sits on the lip of a three-hundred-foot cliff and Irish is still the language of the shop.

destinations.name: Malmö & Skåne
destinations.blurb: Sweden's most mixed city, twenty minutes over the bridge from Copenhagen — a twisting tower on a reclaimed shipyard, falafel better than anywhere in the country, and a beach in the middle of town.

destinations.name: Odense & Funen
destinations.blurb: Hans Christian Andersen's town, rebuilt around a museum that treats his stories as architecture — on an island of manor houses, orchards and thatched villages that Danes call the garden of Denmark.
photos: Odense cobbled old town coloured houses

destinations.name: Stavanger & Preikestolen
destinations.blurb: A harbour of white wooden warehouses and the largest surviving old town of its kind in northern Europe — and two hours away by boat and boot, a flat slab of rock hanging six hundred metres straight over a fjord.

destinations.name: Ephesus & Izmir
destinations.blurb: The best-preserved classical city in the Mediterranean — a marble street running down to a library facade still two storeys high — with a large, secular, seafront Turkish city an hour up the coast to sleep in.

destinations.name: Pamukkale & Hierapolis
destinations.blurb: A hillside of white travertine terraces filled with warm mineral water, stepped down the slope like frozen waterfalls — with a Roman spa city on the plateau above it and a pool you can swim in among its fallen columns.
